newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal local government spending bill rejected.
newsitem.headline: Portugal local government spending bill rejected.

text.p: A Portuguese government bill on local government spending plans was rejected by opposition parties on Thursday and Prime Minister Antonio Guterres planned to address the nation later in the day, officials said.
In a parliamentary vote, opposition parties cast 109 votes to reject the bill against 102 in favour, they said.

The Socialist government has said that opposition proposals for local government financing, which increase the funding received by local authorities, would boost overall public expenditure and lead to tax rises.
The government's bill proposes granting increased powers to local authorities, but does not increase their funding.

Guterres's government was elected in October 1995 after pledging to lead Portugal into the European single currency from the start in 1999 and promising not to raise taxes, but its victory fell four seats short of an absolute majority.

Guterres said in May that he wanted early elections if the main opposition parties pushed through parliament local government spending plans that would lead to tax rises and jeopardise Portugal's entry to the single currency.
A statement from the cabinet said that Guterres would address the nation on television at 1915 GMT. It gave no further details.
Any decision to call early elections would be taken by President Jorge Sampaio.
